Hotel has total 258 rooms and 21 suites which includes some stylish rooms. Tennis and squash courts, swimming pool and a health club are located inside the hotel building. Among the restaurants inside the hotel are, rooftop "Chandni" for Pakistani, "Taipan" and "Marcopolo" for Chinese, a steak house "Jason Steak House" and "the Royal Elephant" for the sea food lovers, also a 24 hours nice coffee shop and a small shopping centre in the lobby. Overall a high standards hotel. This was the first-ever five-star Intercontinental Hotel in Pakistan, and has hosted Queen Elizabeth II, Nelson Mandela, and other world leaders and royalty. It's known for its classic luxury and an array of restaurants including Sakura serving authentic Japanese food on the hotel's top floor, which has views of downtown Karachi.

name: Ramada Plaza Hotel
content: Owned by international hotel chain (Ramada) Wyndham Worldwide. This is considered as airport hotel because of its very close proximity to airport.

name: Aga Khan Hospital
content: This hospital is by far the best and biggest private hospital in the city, with world class medical care though not at an affordable cost but profound professional service. However, the free, government hospitals aren't up to par with what some visitors may be used to.

name: British Deputy High Commission Karachi
content: (Also provides consular services for nationals of the Republic of Ireland and New Zealand in addition to the UK)

name: Ireland
content: (Also see British Deputy High Commission above since they also provide consular services for Irish nationals in addition to the UK)

name: Romania
content: Honorary Consulate (Does not provide consular services. Instead, Romanian citizens in need of assistance should contact the embassy in Islamabad.)

name: Boating
content: You can hire a boat for a 15–20min ride at Kemari boating harbour, which will take you to Manora Island (though not really an island) or tour you around the Karachi harbour. At the southeastern end of Manora island is the tallest lighthouse (28 m high) in Pakistan, which was erected by the British after they captured Karachi's Talpur rulers. The access to lighthouse is unfortunately restricted due to its presence inside the military protected area. Private boats can be hired for around Rs 500-3,000 per hour according to size of boat. If you are also interested in eating fish or crabs, ask the boat owner to arrange some and have a cookout on the boat while you travel. Please avoid taking photographs as it is prohibited when you're touring near the harbour due to its proximity to a Naval base, and other sensitive installations around. Even the boats crew will discourage you to take photos. Aside from the wooden trawlers, ferries are also available. Some captains of boats and ferry offers sea fishing, or even just crabbing but within the harbour. You can spend a romantic evening crabbing in Karachi's coastline beginning at sunset and ending with a delightful crab and seafood feast under the stars in evening. There are also two ferry boats run by government, which run twice daily and can take you to Manora island free of charges. You can also rent larger boats from Kemari boat harbour for longer duration to go further away to other islands such as Bundle Island or Buddo Island but you'll have to heavily negotiate to get a better rate, and try to avoid the touts who would be lurking outside in the parking area. One of the best ways to see Karachi coastline is from the waters of Karachi. Boats in Kemari may offer marvellous tour and views of the Karachi beach and Port of Karachi of varying durations and prices

name: Dumpukht
content: (Marriott Hotel). Live Indian traditional dancer, every night except Monday from 20:00-23:30

name: PC hotel
content: Live band playing all types of music followed by Ghazals from 20:30-23:00. Live Ghazal band from 23:00-01:00

name: Baltit Fort
content: Beautiful old fort that was the seat of the Mirs of Hunza for centuries. Tour guides are knowledgeable and the fort has quite a lot of artefacts to see.

name: Altit Fort
content: This fort is a hundred years older than Baltit Fort and is impressively situated. Not so well restored as Baltit Fort, no museum inside, but still well worth a visit.

name: Eagle's Nest
content: A place up the mountain (near Eagles Nest Hotel Hunza, see the map) with spectacular views of Hunza Valley. Come here to watch the sunset.

name: Hunza Food Pavilion
content: Lal Shehzadi is a local woman who, with her company, makes and serves local food, inexpensive and tasty. You can hear staff in the kitchen talking Burushaski, the local language.

name: Cafe de Hunza
content: Popular with travellers, has free Wifi.

name: Pizza Pamir
content: Great views from the seating area.

name: Sweet Tooth Hunza
content: Restaurant that serves Western food.

name: Tourist Cottage & Restaurant
content: Friendly staff, welcomes you with green tea, recommends sights and places to eat. Same owner as Haider Inn.

name: Hunza Backpacker's Inn
content: Hotel, wifi, hot shower.

name: Haider Inn
content: Homely feel, en suite doubles and dorm rooms with hot water. Fantastic set meal at 8PM Rs125.

name: Darbar Hotel
content: Claims three stars.

name: Eagles Nest Hotel Hunza
content: Mountain-top hotel with spectacular views.

name: Karakoram Air Safari
content: is the scenic air journey offered by PIA

name: Mountaineering, trekking and hiking
content: The area is ideal for mountaineering, trekking and hiking. Permission for mountaineering and trekking for restricted zone is issued by the Ministry of Tourism, Government of Pakistan, Pakistan Sports Complex, Kashmir Highway, Aabpara, Islamabad (Telephone: 92-51-9203509). Fishing permits are issued by the Fisheries Department at Gilgit and Skardu

name: Fishing
content: at Lakes. Fishing permits are issued by the Fisheries Department

name: Hike to Ultar meadow
content: through the steep canyon above the main town that can be seen behind Baltit fort. Great views of the area can be enjoyed, especially of the imposing Lady Finger peak high above the town. As of July 2019, floods have washed away the path on the right hand side of the canyon, therefore it is advisable to hire a guide to show you the way

name: Keenjhar Lake Resort
content: Run by Sindh Tourism Development Corporation, this is the only proper accommodation on the lake. The resort has a total of 24 huts, a good restaurant and a lawn facing the lake with a good sitting area in the evening. Some of the huts are big and others are small. Each is a separate building, with a bed room on the first floor and sitting area and dining rooms on the ground floor. Each hut is equipped with double bed, air-conditioning, LCD cable TV, baths and other basic amenities. It's recommended to book in advance through STDC office in Karachi, nevertheless rooms may also be available for rushed in visitors. The resort has two modern speed boats available for those who want to take a tour in the lake.

name: Desert Hawks Resort
content: A simple lodging facility with some cottages owned by the Pakistani Army, which may also provide rooms to visitors for overnight stay at nominal charges.

name: Faiz Mahal
content: Built by Mir Sohrab Khan in 1798 as the principal building serving as the sovereign's court for the royal palace complex of Talpur monarchs of the Khairpur dynasty.

name: Tomb of Sachal Sarmast
content: It is a beautiful shrine and the resting place of the Sufi poet and great master of Islamic learning Sachal Sarmast, who lived a humble, ascetic life, preferring solitude and composed poetry in Sindhi, Seraiki, Persian and Urdu. Sachal Sarmast's Urs is celebrated on 14th of Ramzan (9th month of Islamic lunar calendar).

name: Kot Diji
content: An Indus Valley Civilization town, dating back to 2500–3500 BCE, is regarded as one of the world's most important archaeological sites, dating back to 3000 BC, older than Moen-jo-daro and Harappa. Excavations made in 1955 unearthed an astoundingly well-organized city with a citadel that testifies to its being the finest fortified town in South Asian subcontinent.

name: Mehrano Wildlife Sanctuary
content: Home to approximately 4,000 big game animals, including blackbuck, Indian gazelle, hog deer, wild boar. Additionally the forest lake boasts resident and migratory birds from Siberia and Europe. There is a reserved place for tourists to see wild boars

name: Jamia Masjid Khairpur
content: If you want to offer the prayer (Salah), go to this grand mosque. You can get Khairpur prayer times by clicking the mosque link.

name: Ahmed Biryani And BBQ
content: It is one of the best restaurant for Foodies.

name: Khaplu Fort
content: Once a palace, now a hotel.

name: Am Tex Waterfall
content: is located at Am Tex Squire, Abdullah Pur. It is the biggest artificial waterfall in Asia. It looks very beautiful at night

name: Forest Park Gatwala:
content: There is a forest park Gatwala 12 km from Khurrianwala. It is very beautiful. It has a lake for boating. It has also a canal. It also has a small zoo. Especially evening scenes are very beautiful in Gatwala Park

name: Canal Park
content: is located at the west bank of Rakh Branch Canal. It is also a good outing place for families

name: Town Center:
content: There is a monument in the centre of the town. This monument was built in the reign of Shair-Sha-Souri. He has also made a well which is situated in police station near monument. He has also made a rest house for passengers which is now converted to Rescue-1122 office by new construction

name: Fatima Jinah Lady Park
content: A small beautiful lady park made for ladies. It is at Jhumra road 1km from bus stop

name: Historical Well:
content: There is a historical well made in the rule of Shair-Shah-Sauri. It is under the supervision of Government. It is situated in Police Station Khurrianwala

name: Ghenta Ghar (clock tower)
content: This is the main market of Faisalabad and it is also the oldest area of Faisalabad. Here you can also find the remains of buildings which mainly belonged to the British Raj before Pakistan came into being. Interestingly, this market has eight bazaars (markets) which together form a "Union Jack" (British flag), being a part of the construction work under the British Raj

name: Swimming:
content: There is a swimming pool near "Bahoo Petrol Pump" Shaikhupura Road. Also another swimming pool is near Gatwala. You can also go to "Butt Water Land" and "Happy Land Water Park" at canal road

name: Night life:
content: Faisalabad has a limited but active night life. To get into the circles with a night life, getting connected with the local elite (for lack of better words) will be useful. Should you manage, there is often something happening each night. You can go to D-Graoun Faisalabad especially at night for shopping and eating

name: Clothing
content: Faisalabad is famous for its cloth and cloth related items throughout the world. It is the best market to buy home furnishings (bedsheets, curtains, towels, etc.),  clothing, and hosiery wear. It is very close to Faisalabad so mainly shopping take place in Faisalabad. There are some big shops for clothing like "Bajwa Garments" and "HAS Garments"

name: Fair Price Shops:
content: You can go to Fair Price shops of any textile mill. Here you can get very economical home furnishings (bedsheets, curtains, towels, etc.), clothing, and hosiery wear

name: Stationery & sweets products:
content: If you want to buy some products related to stationery there are some shops available. You can also buy candies at Millat Traders Khurrianwala. It is situated at Jandwali Road. They deal in all kind of candies and sweets. Soap Stone and its related products made in their factory. They are OEM Service Provider of many things like salanty and candies. They provide Buyer Label service on soap-stone products. You can visit their soap-stone factory (commonly known as Salaty Factory) at Gulshan-e-Ahmed Colony Shaikhupura road Faisalabad

name: Sweets:
content: There is a big shop naming "Hafiz Sweets" where you can find every kind of sweet. It is on Jhumra road. There are other sweets shops such as "Best Sweets" and "Butt Sweets"

name: Ice Cream:
content: "Chaman Ice bar" and "Hafiz Ice bar" are two main shops for ice creams

name: Restaurant:
content: "Canada Hotel", "Five Star Hotel" and "Noshahi Restauren" are best places for BBQ and other Pakistani and Continental dishes in Khurrianwala

name: Biryani/Pilaow:
content: Sundar Baryani is a famous shop for biryani and pilaow. Also Jahangir Murgh Pilow is famous in Faisalabad

name: Samosas & Dahi Bale:
content: Sultani Samosa and Dahi Bale Shop is very famous for its samosas and Dehi Bale in Khurrianwala. You will not find such a delicious samosas around

name: Rabri
content: It is made by mixing peanuts, almonds & many other dry fruits in milk and is very delicious

name: Limo pani
content: It is made up with lemon juice & water

name: Lassi
content: Lassi is the traditional Punjabi drink.  Lassi is available in all parts of the city easily.  It is made using yogurt. The price of one glass or a Piala of Lassi is about Rs.20-30

name: Lāhūt Lā makān
content: A cave in a valley, a spiritual destination next to the shrine of saint Bilawal Shah Noorani. Some authors claim that it was once an important place for Hindu worship, which is consistent with the history of other Hindu sites in the area that were converted to Sufi centers over time.

name: Faizan e Aulia Masjid
content: One of the most beautiful mosques in Khuzdar district, and an important tourist destination. Most people come here to visit the fabulous architecture.

name: Ruins of Takht-i-Bahi
content: in Mardan

name: Bala Hisar Fort
content: in Peshawar

name: Burj Hari Singh
content: Sikh fort founded by Sikh General Sardar Hari Singh Nalwa (no longer exists)

name: Panch Tirath
content: An ancient Hindu site now converted into a park

name: The Sikh Temple
content: at Jogan Shah

name: Gor Khuttree
content: An ancient site of Buddha's alms or begging bowl in Peshawar. Headquarter of Syed Ahmad Shaheed, Governor Avitabile

name: Pakhtu Academy
content: The site of an ancient Buddhist University

name: Ghanta Ghar
content: clock tower in Peshawar

name: Bab-e-Khyber
content: Monument situated at the entrance of the Khyber Pass. The gate is located immediately west of Peshawar, with the historic Jamrud Fort lying adjacent to it

name: Khyber Rifles Museum
content: Located within the Landi Kotal Fort, this fascinating museum tells the story of the Khyber Rifles paramilitary force, with a treasure trove of artifacts and memorabilia.

name: Hub Dam
content: One of Pakistan's largest dams, is a major attraction in the south-west of the park and is a good place for water-based activities. The dam has produced a large reservoir on a river that courses through arid plains and low stony hills. Much of the reservoir's shoreline is steep and stony.

name: Koh Tarash
content: Prehistoric ruins.

name: Ranikot
content: An enormous fortification built on barren hills in the extreme north-eastern part of the park. Ranikot is believed to be one of the largest forts in the world and is a major attraction in the region due to its mind boggling size: the fort’s massive 10-m-high walls of dressed sandstone are 26 km in circumference. Seen from a distance, portions of its ramparts resemble the Great Wall of China, as they dip and turn to the contours of the hills. It was built for bow-and-arrow warfare but it was later enlarged to withstand and cope with firearms. Some attribute its construction to Arabs and some to the then-Persian Governor of Sindh in 836 AD and yet other Sindh archaeologists think that some of the present structure, and especially a small inner fortress about 8 km inside the main gate, was either constructed or renovated in the early 19th century by Talpurs of Sindh. Reasons for its baffling construction in this desolate area are equally diverse and unsettled.The fort’s structure, encircling many hills is long, strong walls are made of gypsum and lime-cut sandstone.

name: Taung
content: Chaukundi style marvellous and beautiful historical tombs.

name: Wildlife Guesthouse
content: They have seven cottages with basic facilities and standby generators. Maintained by Sindh Wildlife. For pre-booking a room, contact Sindh Wildlife Department at +92-21-9920 4951/2.

name: Wildlife Guesthouse
content: They have five cottages with basic facilities. Maintained by Sindh Wildlife. For pre-booking a room, contact Sindh Wildlife Department at +92-21-9920 4951/2.

name: Lahore Fort
content: A huge structure where the Mughal and Sikh rulers built their imperial quarters. It is on the UNESCO World Heritage List. There is a small museum dedicated to the Sikh period of the 18th century. A friendly museum caretaker might agree to take you into the summer rooms underground.

name: Alamgiri Gate
content: The iconic entrance to the fort. Located opposite the Badshahi Mosque.

name: Shah Burj gate
content: Decorated with colored tiles. Known as the "Elephant Gate" because royal elephants would enter here. Just inside the gate is the Hathi Paer (Elephant Path) - a staircase with very wide steps so that an elephant's feet could fit on them while climbing to the upper level of the fort. The fort's wall outside this staircase is decorated with tiles including pictures of elephants. (You will also find the Alamgiri Gate occasionally called the Elephant Gate, because its two columns vaguely resemble elephant feet.)

name: Badshahi Mosque
content: Built by the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb, this was long the largest mosque in the world. Entrance is free, but you will be asked to pay about Rs 20 (Nov 2024) to the shoekeeper upon exit. However, it is not compulsory to pay fee for shoe storage. You can instead bring a bag to carry your shoes in after removing them at the entrance. Try going late at night, when there are few people there. Since mosques are holy places, do not wear shorts to this or any mosque; women are advised to wear long or half-sleeved clothing, and to carry a shawl so they can cover their head. Remove shoes before entering.

name: Tomb of Ranjit Singh
content: Tomb of this Sikh ruler of Lahore. Located next to the square between Lahore Fort and the Badshahi Mosque.

name: Minar-e-Pakistan
content: This tower, sometimes called the "Eiffel Tower of Pakistan", was built on the site where in 1940 the creation of a separate state for Muslims was recognized. Located in a park in front of the Fort and Badshahi Mosque.

name: Wazir Khan Mosque
content: An exquisite tiled mosque located near Delhi Gate.

name: Shahi Hammam
content: A Persian-style bathhouse built in 1635, restored in 2015, and covered with beautiful frescos.

name: Punjab University (Old Campus)
content: Buildings were erected here as early as 1858.

name: National College of Arts
content: Rudyard Kipling's father was the principal here. Offers a thesis show every winter. Kim's Gun is outside the NCA

name: Islamic Summit Minar
content: An obelisk built to commemorate the 1974 Organisation of Islamic Cooperation conference. Located in the Charing Cross roundabout. Few know the presence of a library/museum below the roundabout that is all about the OIC and Islamic Summit and is a treat to visit.

name: Shahdin Manzil
content: An impressive building, dating to 1914.

name: Masonic Temple
content: An impressive old building. Since 1972, no longer used by the Masons.

name: WAPDA House
content: A modern office block, with a glass dome and a roof garden.

name: Lahore Zoo
content: One of the oldest zoos in the sub continent, founded in 1872. The material used in some of the construction even bears the marks of 1853. The Lahore zoo attracts a large crowd throughout the year. Driving east along the Sharah-e-Quaid-e-Azam, just past Charing Cross and opposite the WAPDA House is the main gate of the zoo.

name: Al Hamra Arts council
content: Used for theater and other cultural events.

name: Fortress Stadium
content: An attempt to combine the architecture of a fort like Rohtas with a sports stadium. Many exhibitions held here. The Stadium is the site of the famous Horse and Cattle Show in March. Joyland amusement park is also located here.

name: Shalimar Gardens
content: A three-tiered formal garden built in the 1600s, and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Chauburji Gate
content: An impressive, ornate 4-towered gate dating to 1646.

name: Tomb of Jahangir
content: Built in 1637 for the Mughal emperor Jahangir.

name: Data Durbar
content: A Sufi Muslim shrine to Lahore's patron saint, Hazrat Daata Ganj Bakhsh. This vast modern structure is always filled with people praying, collecting or bestowing alms, or eating at the huge charity 'langar' or soup kitchen.

name: Trafalgar Square
content: A replica of the famous Trafalgar Square in London is located in the Bahria Town suburb. A Mini Egypt and a Zoo are located nearby and also worth a visit.

name: Lahore Museum
content: The largest museum in Pakistan, established during the British Raj in 1864. It displays a complete cross-section of the culture and history of the region with a fine collection of Buddhist art from the Gandhara Period, Islamic artifacts, calligraphy, old manuscripts, arms, costumes and jewelry. John Kipling, father of the writer Rudyard Kipling, was curator in the 19th century and the museum appears in the first chapter of Kim. Unfortunately the presentation is old-fashioned and basic, and captions are sometimes in Urdu only.

name: Tollinton market
content: Built as an exhibition hall and later a market, it now hosts the Lahore City Heritage Museum. Built in 1864.

name: Shakir Ali Museum
content: This museum was actually Shakir's House at 93, Tipu Block, New Garder Town, Lahore, which he made for himself. After his death it was bought by Idara-I-Saqafat-e-Pakistan, and turned into a museum on April 3, 1976. The idea behind it was not only to preserve the great artist's paintings and other masterpieces under one roof but also to open this combination of modern and traditional architecture to the public.

name: Fakir Khana Museum
content: A very large and interesting private Museum known as Faqirkhana lies inside the Bhatti Gate and is worth visiting. The museum houses a variety of old paintings, including some by great masters, original manuscripts in different languages and artifacts from South East Asia and the Indian subcontinent.

name: Mughal Museum
content: An industrial and commercial museum, established in 1950, which is meant to depict country's economic resources both in the form of raw products and worked objects. Its collection is arranged in one gallery and one large hall of the building. The main hall displays a range of variety of material such as well plated musical instruments, table lamps of camel skin from Multan and Bhawalpur, cotton, silken-woolen and embroidered textiles from all important cities of Pakistan.

name: Javed Manzil
content: A museum commemorating Muhammad Iqbal, Pakistan's national poet, who lived in this building for several years before his death in 1938.

name: Gaddafi Stadium
content: Built in 1959, renovated in 1996 and named for the Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi, this has a capacity of 27,000 and hosts international Test matches, and Lahore Qalanders in the T20 Pakistan Super League.

name: Lawrence Gardens & Library
content: Among the biggest gardens of Lahore.

name: Jallo Park
content: Following the canal side road to the east of the city is Jallo Park. It is a large drive-in park with a drive-in zoo and a man-made lake. Spreading over 450 acres, it has expanses of lawns, a forest research centre, a children's park, a small museum and a gift shop. Sozo Water Park is another attraction in this park. Also see Sindbad, Joy Land and Sky Land. It can be visited by road and by rail. A rail car leaves for Jallo Railway Station every half hour.

name: Race Course Park
content: A huge park featuring vast lush grounds, a lake for boating, and a well-maintained jogging track. The park hosts special flower shows during the spring season.

name: Gulshan-e-Iqbal Park
content: A vast park with a lake for boating, a mini-zoo, and recreational rides.

name: Anarkali bazaar
content: Named after a courtesan who was buried alive for loving a prince, is one of the chief shopping areas. Anarkali Bazaar is a treasure-trove, selling virtually everything from handicrafts to transistor radios, women's clothing to refrigerators. It is a maze of lanes and alleys which stretch northwards from the Mall to the Central Museum's end. The bazaars in the old city are the ones people romanticize in literature and films. They consist of tiny alleys, some of which will admit a rickshaw, a string of donkeys or carts- and pedestrians have to leap into doorways to give room. Some alleys are only possible single file.

name: Ichra Bazaar
content: Has the best quality of unstitched silk, cotton and printed material of all sorts.

name: Panorama mall
content: An ideal place to buy formal male clothes. It houses over 1000 shops so you have a large variety of clothes to choose from and that is too at a competitive price.

name: PACE
content: Shopping mall with food, clothes, electronics, movies. Located in Link Road, Model town.

name: Mall of Lahore
content: A very prestigious shopping mall with a super market named green valley mall.

name: Liberty Market
content: A large circular market with hundreds of shops selling clothing, electronics, and so on. A basement shop in Liberty (tell the rickshaw driver it's near H Karim Bakhsh) has good handicrafts, and can be bargained with.

name: Ferozsons Book Centre
content: The oldest book shop in Lahore.

name: Hafeez Centre
content: One of the famous mobile and computer market of the province Punjab, with inexpensive software (pirated), and hardware that can be bargained for.

name: Moon Market
content: Jewellery market, banks, clothes market (mostly for women and children), restaurants.

name: Kareem Block Market
content: Men's wear - casual and formal wear for men of all ages.

name: Chamman Ice Cream
content: A famous ice-cream parlour offering 20 different flavours. They also offer milkshakes and juices of various kinds.

name: Mini Golf
content: Don't miss this place for great open air atmosphere where you can also get sheesha.

name: Chatkhara
content: Serves snack food like samosas, chaat and dahi bhallay

name: Balouchi Sajji
content: One of the best restaurant in Lahore. Best traditionally grilled lamb and chicken in town and after the meal one must have the traditional kawa (green tea)

name: Liberty Market
content: Offers good standard Pakistani food. The mutton karahi at Rs 510 is a popular dish and easily serves two people, while most dishes are half that price. They also offer salads, but see the Stay Healthy section below.

name: Cafe Aylanto
content: Has the best non-Pakistani food in town. Try the shrimp and avocado salad. You can also take your own wine to the restaurant and they'll be happy to serve you; just make sure to inform them on the door, if you have an alcoholic drink with you.

name: Zouk
content: One of Lahore's institutions, despite the distressing decor. It serves a mix of Continental and Thai food. It is highly popular among elites.

name: Freddy's
content: Family-oriented restaurant which has a safe, vaguely continental menu. Freddy's offers an afternoon high tea buffet, which offers a full variety foods and some drinks.

name: Village
content: A vast mud structure which has an all-you-can-eat Pakistani buffet. It's a popular joint to take visiting tourists, as it combines a variety of local foods with good hygiene.

name: Salt n Pepper Grill
content: Owned by the same company as Village, with a fine à la carte menu. Try their sweet lassi.

name: Ziafat
content: Authentic Pakistani food in a buffet style. Their menu is not as grand as Village, but the ambiance is a little more laid-back.

name: Dera
content: Right by the Gaddafi Stadium, sitting on your maniji and gulping lassi, you'll experience a unique truck driver atmosphere here. The food is excellent, but the prices are on the higher end. Favourite among the locals are the assorted naans, chicken mugalahi and mutton chops.

name: Fujiyama
content: It's the only real Japanese restaurant in town, and is considered to be the most expensive.

name: Nandos
content: A globally famous restaurant chain.

name: Costa Nostra
content: Authentic Italian food, overseen by Pak-Italian owners. It has a reservation-only, high-end gourmet experience with a rather well put-together table d'hote, and it has a basement pizzeria where you can't go wrong if want a pizza pie that resembles something from Rome and not Chicago.

name: The Skye
content: One of the highest rooftop restaurants in Lahore, it is on the 19th floor of the Indigo Hotel overlooking the metropolitan of Lahore. MM Alam Road on one side and Liberty on the other. It provides buffet and à-la-carte menu.

name: Loafology Bakery & Cafe
content: Casual dining and gatherings; offers a variety of vegetarian and vegan options.

name: Peeru's Cafe
content: Situated about an hour outside of Lahore. Peeru's, a cafe with an artistic flair. Saturday night is always Jazz Night, Peeru's cafe is really the only place which has live jazz music. Tuesday is Sufi night. Sitting inside, it even feels like some cafe in Venice.

name: Lahore Backpackers Hotel
content: Backpackers hostel. They arrange many trips to local cultural events and offer extremely clean accommodation at very reasonable rates. They can organize parking.

name: Regale Internet Inn
content: The owner, Malik, is a former journalist who can show you some amazing off-the-wall stuff in the city, including weekly trips to Shah Jamal on Thursday nights. It's slightly expensive for what it is, but pretty much the best option in town and worth it for the security and to meet other travelers. It is down an alley and upstairs, behind H. Karim Busch & Sons supermarket. They are pretty good at responding online bookings and often update their blog posts.

name: Mirage Hotel Lahore
content: Internet/Wi-Fi and airport pickup and drop-off.

name: Signature Inn
content: This place is a bit rough around the edges, and not recommended for a single female, but the rooms are clean, large, en suite, air conditioned and the rate includes a simple breakfast.

name: Faletti's Hotel
content: Lahore's true Grand old hotel, built in late 18th century by an Italian and later renovated.

name: Four Points by Sheraton Lahore
content: formerly known as Holiday Inn and Hospitality Inn.

name: Pearl Continental Lahore
content: Pearl Continental is a 4-star hotel.

name: Indigo Hotel
content: Indigo Heights is a 4 star hotel.

name: Hiran Minar
content: A peaceful rural park with a lake and minaret. It used to be favourite hunting sport of the Muslim kings, especially the Mughals. Jehangir erected the pavilion-like monument to commemorate the death of his pet deer (Hiran means deer). It served a double purpose as from its top the hunters could locate the habitations of deer. It is a beautiful picnic as well as a historic spot. A high Bara Dari Ghat is constructed right in middle of a Talab. A man made big lake, boating facility is also available. A good garden lay out is surrounding the place.

name: Charing Cross
content: Lahore's monumental square dating to the British era. Surrounded by historic buildings. It has been renamed to Faisal Square (Faisal Chowk in Urdu/Punjabi)

name: Lahore Art Gallery
content: The Croweaters Gallery

name: Medical tourism
content: is a growing industry in Lahore due to its high quality and low cost, especially in sectors like Dental treatment, Hair transplant, Cosmetic surgery and Open heart surgery

name: Wagah Border Ceremony
content: Grand Trunk Road, Wagah. Daily 4:15 PM or 5:15 PM depending on the season. A patriotic and energetic display of military showmanship between India and Pakistan, known for its loud atmosphere and extended wait times. The experience is unique and memorable, though the long wait can be tiring. Entry is free. If coming from Wagah at the Pakistani border, take a cycle-rickshaw (Rs 15, 3 km) to the Attari station, where you can catch a local bus to Amritsar (Rs 15, 25 km). Taxis also use this route and charge around Rs 200 (800 from the Raja Sansi Airport) for the entire vehicle. (updated July 2024)

name: Mozang Bazaar
content: sells some particularly interesting hand-block printed cloth, tablecloths and bedspreads

name: Xinhua Mall
content: has brands such as Nike, The Body shop, Levis, Cross Roads, Next, Minni Minors and from the local brands we have Ammar Bilal, Nomi Ansari, Out Fitters and Saira Ahsan

name: Readings bookshop
content: in Main Boulevard Gulberg and Variety Books in liberty market are a must see

name: Last word
content: in Gulberg at 32-A, Mian Mehmood Ali Kasoori Road

name: Raja Centre
content: in Gulberg has a good selection of handloom 'khadi' fabric, both stitched and unstitched. Higher end khadi can be bought at the Khaadi shop in Mini Market

name: Fortress Stadium
content: has a huge variety of inexpensive linens, clothes, DVDs

name: Ehsan chappal house
content: has shoes for ladies, also check out Stylo shoes for stylish shoes and clutches/purses

name: Joray Pull
content: is a developing area near airport and Rangers HQ. It's safe and you do a lot of eating activity here along with shopping

name: Levi's
content: products are comparatively cheap as they're produced in Pakistan. A regular pair of trousers in an official retail store will be between 5,000 and 10,000 Rs

name: Phajjay Ke Paye
content: at Red Light Area - Heera Mandi Lahore, is very famous and highly energetic. Those having physical weakness must try this dish

name: Basheer-dar-ul-Mahi
content: at Mazang Chok Lahore - fried fish is served in 2/3 forms. You will see people queued up in lines to get their order here. Don't go if you don't have much time. But this fish is worth waiting this much. Parathas and Lassi at Mazang Lahore - Near the Baheer-dal-ul-Mahi is this very cheap and small scale restaurant. Serves paraths of potatoes, minced chicken, egg and others with Tea or delicious Lassi. Don't miss this at breakfast or anytime you want to have something energetic

name: Gourmet foods
content: is very famous and it has over 100 outlets in Lahore

name: Student Biryani
content: Fortress Stadium. Popular Pakistani food chain that is best known for selling its biryani dish. Has branches all over the city as well in Karachi, Dubai and Sharjah

name: Cakes and bakes
content: is a very good bakery. On the same range: Kashmir bakery, Bon vivant cafe,  Massoms cafe

name: Jalal Sons
content: 12 E main market, Gulberg

name: Kitchen Cuisine
content: in Allama Iqbal town, DHA, Defence, Gulberg, Johar Town, Model Town

name: Rinnas Kitchenette
content: Xblock, DHA, Lahore

name: Iceberg Parlour
content: Aziz Bhatti Rd, Saddar Town. Ice cream

name: Iceland
content: MM Alam Rd, Block B3 Block B 3 Gulberg III. Frozen fruit parfait, ice cream, etc

name: Gelato affair
content: Fortress Stadium Rd. Another ice cream

name: Khan jee dry fruit and home made ice cream
content: Commercial area phase 1, DHA

name: The Hot spot
content: Defence: 19 T block, DHA Phase 2

name: Mexican cafes
content: Chalupa in Samnabad which has many tasty Mexican dishes like taco. There is also a bar with night time disco

name: Kim's snack bar
content: in Samnabad. Lahore second best shawarma

name: Caviar Lounge
content: a bar/club in Royal Palm

name: Club Bhurban
content: in Pearl Continental hotel

name: Uptown LA
content: in Defence R block. The club opens after 11PM at night till 4AM in the morning

name: Cinamoon Coffee lounge and Bakery
content: Sharah e Quaid e Azam, Avari Hotel

name: Gloria Jeans Coffee:
content: Defence: 42Z, Commercial; and Gulberg: 25/2B, Kasuri road

name: Hobnob Cafe:DHA
content: phase 2

name: Jamin Java Cafe:
content: Has three branches in Lahore mainly in Defence, Gulberg and Johar Town

name: World Fashion cafe
content: Kasuri road, Gaulberg, Lahore

name: Nadia cafe
content: Pearl Continental Hotel, Sharah e Quaid e azam

name: Jhoker Jo Daro
content: Another archaeological site in the district.

name: Mausoleum of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto
content: The mazar is notable for containing the graves of the Bhutto family members. People from all over Pakistan come to this mazar throughout the year.

name: Sukarno Tower
content: Built in the middle of the town, this monument was presented by the Indonesian president Sukarno on visit to Larkana.

name: Zulfiqar Bagh
content: Take an evening stroll in the park.

name: Asia
content: A good hotel with A/C rooms, free Wi-Fi Internet, and a restaurant.

name: Paris Inn
content: This hotel is yet another good place to stay in town.

name: Green Palace Hotel
content: Reasonably clean and spacious room along the main stretch. Among the cheapest options in the area.

name: Gadani ship-breaking yard
content: World's third largest ship breaking yard after Alang and Chittagong in terms of volume, located across a 10-km-long beachfront of Arabia sea. Gadani has an annual capacity of breaking up to 125 ships of all sizes, including supertankers which are dismantled and recycled, often with bare hands and welding torches. Gadani is the world's leading ship breaking yard in terms of efficiency. At Gadani, a ship with 5,000 LDT is broken within 30 to 45 days, whereas in Alang and Chittagong, it takes, on average, more than six months for breaking a vessel of the same size. Tourists are not usually welcome, but some travelers have been able to sweet talk the gate-keeper and get amazing photos of massive ships being dismantled for parts and steel. There are many breaking yards stretching for miles, so start at one end and try your luck until you have success.

name: Takht-i-Bahi
content: Exceptionally well-preserved ancient Buddhist monastery dating back to the Indo-Parthian Kingdom. The monastery was founded in the 1st century CE, and was in use until the 7th century. The site is considered among the most important relics of Buddhism in the whole region. Takht-i-Bahi was has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1980.

name: Bacha Khan Monument
content: Dedicated to Abdul Ghaffar Khan, Pashtun freedom fighter and independence activist against British colonial rule in India known for his nonviolent opposition and lifelong pacifism.

name: Guides Memorial
content: Built in 1892 to honour fallen soldiers who fought during the 1879 Siege of the British Residency in Kabul.

name: Swat Museum
content: Contains Gandharan statuettes and friezes depicting the lives of the Buddha, pre-Buddhist artefacts and an ethnographic gallery with traditional carved Swati furniture, jewellery and embroideries.

name: Butkara Stupa
content: A sacred area for Buddhism, near the city of Saidu Sharif, excavated under the name Saidu Sharif I, is, at the foot of the mountains that separate the river valley Saidu from that of the river Jambil, in the Swat District.

name: Khari Sharif Darbar
alt: Darbar Sharif Hazrat Pir Shah Ghazi R.A.
content: A place of religious importance, well known due to the shrines of Sufi Baba Peer-e-Shah Ghazi and Mian Mohammad Buksh.

name: Mangla Fort
content: Reportedly you need special permission from the Pak Army or Mangla Special Authority to visit, it consists of a historic Gakkar fort and one-room museum, monument to Pres Sharif, and overlook of Mangla Dam Lake. Nearby are the massive dam (which is the 6th largest in the world) and bridge that connects Punjab Province to Pakistan-occupied Kashmir with a sign denoting such and where Alexander the Great is claimed to have crossed the Jhelum River. Might make for an interesting photo-op if it doesn't draw attention from police/military.

name: Ramkot Fort
content: Fort built over the site of an old Hindu temple. Three sides of this hill top are surrounded by River Jhelum (Mangla Lake). During excavations relics of the 5th - 9th century AD have been discovered. It is on the opposite side of the lake from Mirpur. A 10-minute trip by road from Mirpur leads to Sukhian and nearby Mangla View Resort/Army Water Sports Club from where boats are available to access Ramkot Fort. It takes 45 minutes to reach there.

name: Baghsar Lake and Fort
content: A picturesque lake in the Samahni Valley often inhabited by migratory fowl and lilies, with an old Mughal fort from the mid-18th century overlooking it. It is said that the Emperor Jahangir fell ill on his way back from the Kashmir Valley and died here. But this area is supposedly closed due to its proximity to the Line of Control.

name: Bhutto Park
content: If you just want some downtime by the lake or some views of the dam, this is a good place.

name: Mangla View Resort
content: A lakeside resort offering parasailing and jet skiing and other water sports on Mangla Dam Lake. It is designed for both Pakistani military personnel and civilian use.

name: Jari Kas
content: Amusement centre with boat and kiddie rides, though the safety of some might be questionable. Also views of the lake.

name: Crown Plaza
content: Main shopping centre for Mirpur, a multi-storey glass building.

name: Nafees Quality Food
content: Pakistani eatery with salad, samosas, and a large selection of bakery items.

name: Grand Regency Hotel Mirpur
content: 6-storey established hotel with pool, restaurant, bar, wifi.

name: Holidays In Kashmir
content: Moderately-priced hotel with restaurant and wifi and good views of the dam.

name: Undrah Inn Hotel
content: Semi-modern looking hotel with WiFi.

name: Hotel Jabeer
content: Hotel with restaurant, bar, and wifi, right next to the Grand Regency Mirpur. It has kind of gone downhill over the years.

name: Chitorri graveyard
content: This is the historical ancestral graveyard of the Talpur Mirs, the former rulers of Mirpurkhas. Impressive tombs decorated with beautifully carved calligraphy dating back to the 17th and 18th centuries have very interesting and wonderful sandstone architecture and monuments.

name: Kahu Jo Darro
content: The oldest historical site in Mirpurkhas is of course the Buddhist archeological site, Kahu Jo Darro. A Buddhist stupa was excavated from this site. However, due to negligence by the government authorities, nothing interesting is left on the site for general tourists. Archeologists and scientific investigators, however, can still find interesting remains for their research.

name: Mirpur Khas Museum
content: Antiques and armoury belonging to the Talpur rulers are on display in the museum. The museum also serves as a library.

name: Shiva Mandir
content: There are a few old Hindu temples in Mirpur Khas. Shiva Mandir is the oldest.

name: Sufyania Food Centre
content: Considered to be among the best dining places in town, it has an air-conditioned dining area with Pakistani, Continental and Chinese dishes on the menu along with some barbecue and fast food.

name: Aftab Restaurant
content: Famous in town for its Karahi dishes, it has both chicken and mutton Karahi. The cost for one person is only Rs 180 for a chicken plate and Rs 280 for mutton, and the portions are more than enough for a person to eat.

name: Cafe Shiraaz
content: Quality food; also locally famous for tasty tea and patties.

name: Mehboob Restaurant
content: Famous in town for its Karahi dishes, both chicken and mutton Karahi.

name: Bisma Hotel
content: A centralised hotel with total 17 air-conditioned rooms, all with attached baths, free Wi-Fi, cable TV, fridge and other basic amenities. A restaurant is located inside the hotel. Overall, Cleanest, most comfortable guest house in town and the only female-friendly hotel in the city, guarded by security guards.

name: Hotel Marhaba
content: Has both single and double, air-conditioned and non-air-conditioned rooms, all with cable TV, attached bath, free Wi-fi.

name: Hotel Mehran
content: Total 9 rooms, all air-conditioned, with cable TV, free Wi-Fi, attached bath, generator, and other basic amenities.

name: Al-Pine Guest House
content: No Wi-Fi, only 6 air-conditioned rooms with cable LCD TV and attached baths.

name: Gadi Bhit
content: is by far the only attraction in town thus is the most visited and popular site of the town. It is the highest elevation point of the town built on a sandhill and gives a breathtaking panoramic view of the Mithi town.

name: Naukot Fort
content: Historic fort, dating back to 1814.

name: Muslim Taj Restaurant
content: A basic restaurant in town but have some good food.

name: Diamond Restaurant
content: A good restaurant in town in the centre of town popular both among locals as well as visitors, serve some good Pakistani food especially Karahi dish.

name: Diamond Hotel
content: Both Air-conditioned and non air-conditioned rooms available with cable TV and attach baths. A basic lodging, located in the centre of town.

name: Desert Rest and Guest House
content: Provides a big lodging facility in town. Have 10 rooms, all air-conditioned except 2 in the guest house located in the centre of town all equip with cable TV, attach bath, free Wi-Fi and generator. The same hotel have a guest house located on top of the hill of Gadi Bhit, also in Mithi town with total 4 air-conditioned rooms , all equipped with cable TV, attach bath, free Wi-Fi and generator. Must book in advance or check the availability on date you want to move in. Both of the lodgings have on-site kitchen for serving the guests and may cook food according to your requirement.

name: Muslim Taj Hotel
content: A basic lodging, located in the centre of town. Both Air-conditioned and non air-conditioned rooms, total 7, available with cable TV and attach baths.

name: Marvi Guest House
content: Centrally air conditioned, run by Sindh Tourism Development Corporation however have only two rooms but good one in town. Cable TV, attach baths, Air-conditioned, Wifi, as well as kitchen and dinging area for serving the guests and may cook food according to your requirement. A foreigner friendly lodging facility in town. Have open sitting area outside in lawns as well a large parking area. Huts in guest house are made like traditional Thari houses. Recommended to book in advance or check the availability on date you want to move in.

name: The Buddhist Stupa
content: Visible from a great distance, this is the highest and most prominent structure in Mohenjo-daro. It was built atop the citadel mound long after the fall of the ancient city; it is from the Kushan Empire, 1st to 4th centuries CE, while all of the other excavated ruins are from 2,600-1,900 BCE. It is believed that the Buddhist Stupa was built over an older Hindu temple.The stupa is shown on Pakistani twenty rupee notes.

name: The Great Hall
content: The Great Hall is a large building and is believed to have been a granary; it has what appears to have been a loading platform for carts transporting grain and a ventilation system to prevent spoilage. An alternate theory is that it was a public hall; the actual function of the building has not been determined.

name: The Great Bath
content: A 2.4-m-deep, 12-m-long, and 7-m-wide pool in the centre of higher settlement is the best-known structure of Mohenjo-daro. It is made of fine baked waterproof mud bricks and a thick layer of bitumen (natural tar – presumably to keep water from seeping through the walls), which indicates that it was used for holding water. Many scholars have suggested that this huge deep bath could have been a place for ritual bathing or religious ceremonies. It is the earliest public water tank of the ancient world. Adjacent to it is a well that was used to supply water to the bath.

name: Assembly Hall
content: This brick pillared structure of approximately 27.5 m² is thought to may have been an assembly hall, a place for people to sit for meetings and social gatherings. Some believe it to be prayer hall or a palace.

name: College of Priests
content: A unique large open space and courtyard lying to the east of the Great Bath, this large building has several rooms and three verandas, with two staircases leading to the roof and upper floor. It is thought to have been either a college for priests or the residence of a high official.

name: Mohenjo-daro Archaeology Museum
content: The museum was inaugurated in 1967, and contains relics found at the archaeologic site. The relics include weapons, engraved seals, kitchen utensils, sculptures and terracotta toys. Jewellery and other ornaments are showcased on the first floor and illuminated in natural light while heavy stones found during excavation are kept as well. A wall on the first floor is illustrated with a conjectural yet impressive view of the ancient city.

name: Archaeology Rest-house
content: Renovated accommodation is run by Pakistan's archaeological department is overall, ideal for a stay overnight and available at affordable rates. They can also provide pick and drop to/from Larkana or Badah station via car. The rest house has nine rooms with attached baths. Three air conditioned rooms, double bed, TV, and sofas are on the first floor while six non-air conditioned rooms with two single beds in each room on ground floor. Has a cafeteria, sitting area in lounge as well a big hall to accommodate large group of people for overnight stays. Cafeteria can prepare a meal according to your taste but may charge Rs 500 per person for lunch or a dinner meal while Rs 200 for breakfast. It is advised to book in advance.

name: Play Kabati:
content: A number of villagers play Kabati during free time, mostly in season of rain and wind

name: Sindhi Biryani:
content: A dish popular in Sindh

name: Busri:
content: A type of Desi roti made of two layers of roti filled with sweet and  butter

name: Desi Lasi:
content: It is most common drink in the village, commonly made from milk of buffalo, sometimes from milk of cow and also goat. Most of the villagers drink it at the time of lunch during summer season but also in other seasons but less commonly

name: Ruins of Multan Fort
content: The Multan Fort on a high mound of earth which separated it from the old branch of the river Ravi. There are now only remnant of this old fort, which was considered as one of the best fort (defense wise) built in the sub-continent. The fort was destroyed when the British took over. During its heydays the fort walls were almost 1.6 km long. The fort is in the middle of the city, close to Multan Cricket Club (MCC) next to Shah Rukn-e-Alam’s Mazar. The huge sprawling ancient complex had seen kings and empires fall or rise before its huge walls. Its initial origins are disputed, but the site was destroyed by the British garrison stationed here during the Raj. There is a park called the Fort Qasim Park. It has some memorials from the Raj era apart from having some electric rides as well. On to the western sight of the fort there is a place called 'Damdama'. It provides a wonderful viewpoint of the city. Try locating an art shop called Nigar Khana on the left as you walk your way towards the Damdama entrance. It is, for unknown reason, located underground. It's a cool shop though with a large collection of traditional Multan handicrafts. Plans are underway to renovate or build a new damdama.

name: Pak Gate
content: This gate named Pak Gate not due to Pakistan, but because of the Saint Hazrat Musa Pak Shaheed. When he died on 33rd Shahban 1010 H, Firstly he was buried in Uch Shareef near his Father Syed Hamid Gunj Buksh. Then when his son saw his Grand Father in Dream Instructing him to get Musa out from his foot side, then he was buried again at "Moza Mungay Hatti". After 15 years his son have another dream who lives in Multan to give Musa back to Multan. Your followers have full faith on you. So, they bring you to Multan. The Gate used to bring your body at that time is still called Pak Gate. 90 m (300 feet) inside Pak Gate you will find the Mazar of Hazart Musa Pak Shaheed.

name: Haram Gate
content: The Gate used to bring your "Haram" is still there and called Haram Gate.

name: Delhi Gate
content: This Gate is named "Delhi" as this faces towards Delhi in India and the road leads towards Delhi. During Mughal Period, when ever the Kings or State Guests visits Multan they entered through this gate.

name: Doulat Gate
content: This City Gate is vanished in early days. Only the name is alive & the place where it was to be. It is thought that the Gate called "Doulat Gate", because of the Mazar of "Pir Doulat Shah" which is on the front of the Gate. The Mazar is still there and people come and pay visits. Now due to modernization and enhancements of circular road across the city this "Mazar" comes between the two roads and only the tomb area left. The Green Tomb of the Mazar is now between the two busy roads.

name: Bohar Gate
content: This Gate faced towards the River Ravi. Once when Multan was a busy river port. This Gate is the main entrance for the food supply and communication. The gate called Bohar because out side this gate there are too many "Bohar" trees. Now with the passage of time the river changed its way and the trees cut down. Now you can see the commercial centers around Bohar Gate.

name: Lohari Gate
content: In urdu "Loha" means iron. The gate named Lohari because many Lohari (ironsmiths) live outside of this gate, and they have their workshops there.

name: Hindu temples in Multan
content: The most important place of the Hindu period was the "Sun Mandir" (Mulasthana in Sanskrit). It was the most important place of worship throughout the South Asia as referred to in many books. It was situated on one of the old Fort. There is however no trace of it now. "Suraj Kund" (the pool of sun) is about 8 km (5 miles) to the South of Multan on the Bahawalpur Road. It was a pond 40 m (132 feet) in diameter and 3 m (10 feet) deep when full of water. Sawn Mal the Sikh Diwan surrounded it with an octagonal wall. It was a place of pilgrimage till 1947 and two fairs were held here annually. One on the 7th of the Vanishing moon of Bhadon, and the other on the 7th of the rising moon of Magh, the numbers having references to the seven hours of the Sun's Chariot, according to the Hindu belief of the seven Rishies.

name: Sawi mosque
content: Sawi Mosque is the oldest mosque of Multan situated in Mohalla Kotla Tolay Khan Outside Lohari Gate. It is supposed to be one of the oldest mosques, which still exists though it has no roof now and most of its decorations have been damaged; glazed blue tiles were profusely used for ornamentation. Parts are still intact

name: Mausoleum of Shah Rukn-e-Alam
content: On top of a small hillock, behind the old ruins of Multan Fort, the Mazar and its majestic dome is the first landmark visible when you enter proper Multan. Shah Rukn-e-Alam (1251-1335) was a Sufi saint in Multan. He was revered by his followers, and to this date thousands of pilgrims from all over Pakistan come to Multan to pay homage. He was the grandson and successor of another great Sufi Shaikh Baha-Ud-Din Zakariya, whose Mazar is also near this one.

name: Clock Tower
content: Called the "Ghanta Ghar" in the Urdu language, it is the landmark of the old city. It was built during colonial times. The clock tower square has undergone renovation and is set to become the major landmark of Multan.

name: Nishtar Medical College
content: The college campus is an old and traditional building. It symbolizes Islamic architecture with central quadrangular.

name: Hussain Agahi Bazar
content: This is more of an all-in-one bazar. Try sampling some local sweets near a shop at its entrance. For the handicraft lovers, walk up the stairs to the first arcade on the right. There is a nice handicraft shop on first floor. Walk further into the bazar and you come across shops of all sorts. the first street down the left is particularly interesting. Here you can find oils of about a hundred plant and animal sources. They even prepare an 'oil cocktail' for you depending on the purpose you want it for. Ask for oil for falling hair and you see three different oils being mixed up with exact proportions. And they work too. A further walk forward on the same road brings you to the spice bazar. Try some nuts if you want. Kalay Manddi is another site ahead, famous for its cut-piece cloth and fabric shops. Moreover, you can find separate sub-bazars or streets naming Sarafa Bazar, Choorian (Bangles in English) bazar.

name: Cantonment Park
content: A boutique park with sub-sections of theme gardens, there is a Japanese garden, palm garden, rose garden a cactus garden so on and so forth. There is an artist corner, A theatre performance area, and a small library. There are separate open air gyms for males and females. It also has a 3-km long clay jogging track with soft music playing all along.

name: Chaman Zar Askari Lake Park
content: A large park with an artificial lake, paddle boats and some electric rides. If you are lucky there is a carnival happening with artists from different parts of the world performing

name: Multan Museum
content: Contains a fine collection of coins, medals, postage stamps of the former State of Bahawalpur, manuscripts, documented inscriptions, wood carvings, camel-skin paintings, historical models and stone carvings of the Islamic and Pre-Islamic period

name: Chenab River Bank
content: Take a boat ride along the river Chenab. For this you will have to drive toward Muzzaffargarh. Alternatively, take a minibus towards Muzzaffargarh from Dera Adda (the minibus station). costs around Rs30. Get off after you cross the Chenab bridge. Take the trail towards left and after a short walk you'll be to reach at the resort where boats will be leaving every now and then. Named as Chenab Park,this is a great site for camping and barbeque. There used to be fishing but not anymore now. It's a great family outing and a picnic spot on the occasions of Eid and other national festivals.

name: Camel skin lamp shades and other handicrafts
content: look for the award winning Naqqash family business. Nigar Khana at the city damdama has a cool handicraft shop at its basement.

name: Jindu Champ Markaz (Ribs and BBQ)
content: A very unique two step BBQ process. Right in the action area of ghanta ghar

name: Tasty Restaurant
content: Serves good quality local food at good prices. Good seating as well. it is on international standards. Their speciality is "Karahi" made with chicken or mutton

name: Fast Food
content: There are quite a few international fast food chains in Multan as well. Pizza Hut is in uptown area of Gulgasht. KFC and Subway are to be found around the high court area in the Cantonment. Pizza parlors are very popular in Multan. Try PizzaTrack near Kutchehri or Papa Gino's in the Cantonment area. Home delivery is always free. Some of the local fast food chains are to be found in the Gulgasht area. A branch of McDonald's has been opened in Cantonment area of Multan.

name: Uptown eateries
content: Most of the uptown eateries are to be found at the Gulgasht area. Try MUX for continental and Jhok for Pakistani food. If you are looking for Mongol cuisine, try "Mongol Dastarkhawn" at Nawan Sheher

name: Zanzibar
content: Good atmosphere.

name: Nawab da hotle
content: It serves special goat meat with spinach and lentils in a village like environment. A favourite with inter-province truckees and multanis alike

name: Khan Restaurant aka Taj Hotel
content: The most authentic lunch in town. For mutton lovers, mutton joints in a thick balck-pepper curry is famous, tastes different and authentic. Does not have reservations and can fill in early for lunch.

name: MUX
content: MUX is the IATA code for Multan Airport. It serves a variety of cuisines

name: Jhok
content: Traditional food in a traditional setting. Expensive.

name: Dahi ballay (curd with mix vegetables) and Gol Gappay
content: Dahi ballay (sour curd with mix vegetables) and gol gappay are a must have in Multan. These are best had at a parking of a local cinema at Nawan Shehr

name: Khara Soda
content: Available at some of the herbalists in and around Ghanta Ghar.

name: RubRee
content: Don't forget to enjoy the sweet drink that is prepared by condensed milk. Available on "Ghanta Ghar" (Clock Tower).  Caution: Dangerous for diabetics.

name: Rus Milaee
content: The "Rus Milaee" is prepared with milk & sweets. Available in most of the sweet shops around town. The best can be found near "Ghanta Ghar" (Clock Tower) & Hussain Agahi Bazar.  Caution: dangerous for diabetics.

name: Ramada Multan
content: Decent 3-star hotel in the city center. Fair prices, nice rooms. Staff is friendly.

name: Sindabad Hotel
content: Good hotel, clean rooms. A/C. Minibar. Cable TV. This is probably the best hotel in the city.

name: Fiesta Inn Hotel & Resorts
content: International direct dial telephone, 27 inch LCD screen TV with satellite channels, Mini Bar, Walk-in closet, Luxury marble bathrooms equipped with a hair dryer and telephone, Central air conditioning with temperature control.

name: Comfort Inn Guest House
content: 10 rooms with en suite bathroom. Pakistani dishes can be ordered onsite. Nearby parking is available and security guards watch the premises. The hotel is a 2-minute drive to Pearl City.

name: The First Hotel
content: In the centre of Multan city, a 20-minute drive from airport.

name: Shrine Mai Maharban
content: A shrine 900 years old near Children Hospital Multan

name: Bahauddin Zakaria
content: The tomb is on top of the old city hillock, behind Shah Rukn-e-Alam's Mazar. South Punjab's largest university is named after this Sufi saint, Bahauddin Zakariya University

name: Eidgah
content: Historic Eidgah in Multan is a part of beautification of the ancient city of saints and revival of its archaic originality. The 268-year old Eidgah, spread over five acres near the LMQ Road, was built in 1735. The architectural specialty of the building is that it is the only edifice having a bulbous dome in southern part of Punjab

name: Myrters Memorial
content: Yadgar-e-Shuhada is a wonderfully landscaped garden with a memorial commemorating the recipients of Nishan-e-Haider, Pakistan's top military award. Its along Shershah Road in the cantonment area. It has a nice sitting place and a popular Fort Bakers nearby

name: Cricket
content: You may be able to catch a game at the Multan Cricket Stadium, which is a traditional venue for a test match and a one-day international every cricket season, which runs from September to February in Pakistan. Cricket has a huge following here, as anywhere in Pakistan. The national captain and star batsmen Inzamam-Ul-Haq is a local boy, and any game sets the town into a frenzy of excitement. ODIs are well attended, sell out crowds. For an "at ease" experience, go to a day at the test. Moderate crowds will make it a much more enjoyable experience. The Multan pitch is one of the flatest in the world, so batting feasts are the norm. Good viewing!

name: Retail stores
content: Multan has three main shopping districts. Saddar Bazzar, Hussain Agahi and Gulgasht. While there is no big supermarket, tourists and foreigners do their shopping from CSD plaza in Cantonment, Prince Departmental store in Saddar (there is a fine supermarket at the basement where you can get all the imported groceries) and Panda on Bosan Road. Sharif Plaza near the city courts has garment retail shops that sell at a bargain. Food Festival is a local chain of convenience stores with main branch at Nishtar Chowk. HTH stores are located in Shahruknealam colony and Garden town

name: Hussain Agahi
content: is a huge but congested market that sells almost anything, famous for local textiles, electronics, spices, carpets, handicrafts, pottery, and the famous Multani halwa. Mind you that without negotiating, you will not get a good deal. Almost everyone are selling the same items, so finding a bargain is quite easy. Haggle for everything you want

name: Brands and textiles
content: Most of the brands are found at Chenone Tower at Abdali Road and Pace at Bosan Road. Feb-March is usually the big sales season

name: Blue Tiles
content: Multan is very famous for its beautiful blue tiles, used in bathrooms and other areas of house/building for decoration

name: Pottery
content: Multani pottery is very famous all over Pakistan, used as decoration, especially vases

name: Quality suitings
content: There are also good local tailors who can wrestle up a fine tunic-trouser combo in fair time. Nice prices

name: Multani Jewellery
content: Very well known all over Pakistan due to its uniqueness of designs, colours and sizes, especially "Multani Har". Hassan Arcade on Nusrat Road has a whole square of Goldsmiths

name: Multani Mitti
content: Multani clay' is used as mud mask

name: Multani Shoes
content: Very famous and traditional shoes, worn during weddings and festivals usually. Look for shops near Ghanta Ghar

name: Mangoes
content: Multan is known as the city of mangoes for a reason. The mango season, whilst stifflingly hot for non regional visitors, affords an amazing treat. Multan produces the juiciest, thickest and the most succulent mangoes in the world. Worth an international flight alone... almost! There are many types of mangoes in Pakistan, including "SindhRi", "anwar rittol", "langRa" , "Chonsa", and "doosairi". Each of them is different in taste, size, quality of pulp etc

name: Multani Sohan Halwa
content: Special dessert of Multan (sometimes mistaken as Habshi Halwa). It is made of sugar, pure ghee and flour and then jeweled with nuts and pistachios. It can be had at most of the tourist spots and sweets shops . Visit Qadeerabad if you want to see it made fresh and indulge in its flavour when it is dished out right off the stove

name: The Mall
content: The Mall is the main strip of Murree with shops, markets, hotels and restaurants. It is the main focal point of Murree and the center of major economic activities. Once a historical central area, is today full of shops selling a multitude of things for the tourists as well as the main point to stroll, eat, sleep and meet people who come to visit Murree from all over the country.

name: Kashmir Point
content: the highest place in Murree.

name: Pindi Point
content: a chairlift runs up to here.

name: Shangrila Resort Hotel Murree
content: A nice and quiet get-away high up in the pine trees, has a restaurant, a grill, a tobacco bar, and a billiards room. Also have several individual cottages, located in a secluded corner of the premises.

name: Jawa Hotel
content: This is off of the mall, up the hill from one of the last roundabouts in town (heading uphill). This hotel takes credit cards and has internet access. Rooms are typical world 3-star class.

name: 34 Morning Side
content: The suites are equipped with internet, flat-screen television, and mini-bar. The hotel also has an amazing terrace, gym, pool table, foosball, and caram board. It also houses a mini-cinema.

name: Hotel Metropole
content: One of many good hotel in town.

name: Usmania Hotel
content: In off season, a decent room will cost around Rs. 500. In June-Aug. peak season costs around Rs. 8,000.

name: PC Bhurban
content: PC Bhurban is the top of the line is the only five star hotel in town. Hotel is 25 minutes drive away from Murree proper. Over crowded by day time visitors during summer seasons. The entry fee for the hotel is Rs. 500 per person for visitors which is fully redeemable while room booking, at restaurants and shops located inside the hotel.

name: Red Onion
content: is a chain restaurant on the main Mall road. Established in 1993, pioneer of "Buy one pizza & get the second one absolutely free", this restaurant offers a wide range of cuisines not offered anywhere else in the vicinity, i.e. Mexican, Italian, Chinese, Pakistani and Continental. Prices are moderate, ambiance is modern and customer service is very friendly

name: Saffron
content: An elegantly decorated restaurant with stunning views of the surrounding hills and valleys. Saffron offered the ultimate personalized culinary experience. The menu is a blend of continental and local favorites including our very own rendition of the ever-popular chicken karahi and chicken makhani. Saffron lies overlooking crisscrossing paths, beautiful hills and valleys. The restaurants outdoor patio allows you to dine under the roof of the world, in the most breathing natural surroundings our part of the world has to offer

name: Angeethi - the Grill
content: is next to the Huqqa Pani lounge and follows the same earthen traditional theme. So after relaxing in the lounge, you can come and watch our chefs prepare a variety of mouthwatering barbeque dishes. The beautiful backdrop and the traditional ambiance, combined with the delicious food make dining at The Grill an occasion to remember

name: Ayubia
content: is about 26 km from Murree, (Khairagali, Changlagali, Khanspur and Ghora Dhaka, these four mini resorts spread over an area of 26 km have been developed into a resort complex called Ayubia). In addition to riding trails, hiking places and picnic spots, Ayubia has a chair lift at Ghora Dhaka, which attracts visitors to enjoy scenic beauty of Pine Hills. The bracing air of the surrounding mountains of Nathia Gali is as pure as fresh spring water

name: AJK Assembly, AJK Supreme Court, Mosque Assembly Secretariat, Kh. Khurshid Tomb
content: Important provincial landmarks

name: Red Fort Muzaffarabad
content: There are two historical forts on opposite sides of the Neelum River. Red Fort and Black Fort The construction of the Red Fort was finally completed in 1646 by Sultan Muzaffar Khan, the founder of Muzaffarabad city. After the Mughals took over Kashmir, the fort lost its importance. The Mughals were more interested in Kabul, Bukhara, and Badakshan. During the period of Durrani rule, however, the fort again once again assumed its importance. Maharaja Gulab Singh and Rambir Singh, the Dogra rulers, reconstructed and extended the fort for their political and military operations. Towards the middle of 1947, the Dogra forces left, leaving the fort abandoned. The architecture of the fort shows that great experts in design and structure participated in its construction. It is surrounded on three sides by the Neelum River formally known as the Kishenganga River. The northern part of the fort had terraces with steps leading to the bank of the river. The eastern side was very well protected from the hazards of flood waters, but some parts on the north side have suffered damage. There used to be an inn at the entrance to the fort, but only traces of that structure remain now.

name: Jalalabad Garden
content: Somewhat of an attempt at a botanical garden. Lots of tulips when in season. Also various types of fowl roaming grounds. And one cannot beat the views.

name: Patikka
content: 19 km from Muzaffarabad, is a gateway to the Neelum Valley. There is also a mini zoo and a fish hatchery. The Tourism Department has constructed a Tourist Rest House here, which is very popular.

name: Pir Chinasi
content: Due to its scenic beauty, velvet green plateaus and wonderful climate, it wins admiration of nature lovers. The view of the summit of the mountain peaks spell bounds a tourist. Devotees of Saint Shah Hussain Bukhari, take pilgrimage to rejuvenate their adust heart. The adjacent Pirchinassi, phawna da Danna and the areas in the bottom of Pirchinassi are also worth seen and ideal for hiking, trekking and camping activities. Tourism Department has also constructed a tourist lodge at Saran.

name: Shaheed Gali Tourist Rest House
content: is 1,640 m above sea level about 16 km west of Muzaffarabad. From Shaheed Gali a trek of 4 km leads towards a spot namely "Sri Kot". A tourist is bound to be fascinated by the serenity for the backdrop of the area. A tourist Rest House is available for accommodation at Shaheed Gali.

name: Subri Lake
content: Scenic viewpoint along Jhelum River.

name: Makra Choti
content: 12,000 ft mountaintop vista among the clouds.

name: Dhani Waterfall
content: Not only is the waterfall an attraction, but the Neelum River Valley in which it is located is (perhaps the highlight). Supreme alpine scenery. At 15 m, this is the highest waterfall in the valley. But if you keep going 103 km from Muzaffarabad up the valley, there is another fall called Kundle Shahi

name: Chikar Highland Resort
content: is a beautiful summer station at a distance of 46 km from Muzaffarabad on top of the mountain. The outstanding features of this beautiful place are its climate and sceneries. 10 km from Chikkar is another worth seen hill station in the middle of dense green pine forests and is linked by a fair weather road.

name: Al Baik Food Park
content: Here you can have some chicken skewers by the river.

name: Agha G Palace
content: Nice views over the city

name: Muzaffarabad Inn
content: Family guest house equipped with all basic necessities. Neat and clean. Rental cars, tourist guide and free open area car parking available. Laundry, wifi, views of bridge and AJK gov buildings.

name: Orash Lodge Guest House
content: Rooftop veranda, restaurant, wifi, laundry. May not always have optical cleanliness, but you may get to use a TV with rabbit ears again.

name: Pearl Continental
content: Five star hotel. Maybe you'll end up rooming next to a head of state. Free breakfast, restaurant, pool, hot tub, gym, laundry, wifi. Grounds and views and atrium are nothing to shake a stick at.

name: Sangam hotel
content: Balconies with views of Neelum River and nearby hills and whatever townspeople decide to throw on their roofs. Restaurant, wifi. Broken furniture and washroom accessories.

name: West End Guest House
content: Economical, kind of like staying in someone's house. Clean toilet, wifi. No restaurant, no views.

name: Handicrafts
content: Carpets, silk woolen clothing, woolen shawls, wood carving, Papier Mashie, rugs

name: Other products and fruits
content: mushrooms, honey, walnuts, apples, cherry, medicinal herbs & plants, resin, Deodar, Kail, Chir, Fir, Maple and Ash Timbers, etc

name: Gori Temple
content: The temple is adorned with Jain religious imagery and the frescos are the oldest among all Jain temples in this region.

name: Bhodesar Mosque
content: Constructed in 1505 CE by Mahmud Begada, the most prominent sultan of Gujarat. Gujarat was an independent kingdom established in the early 15th century in Gujarat, and is now a state of India. The architecture of mosque is of Jain and Isamic style and is still being used for prayers.

name: Karoonjhar Mountains
content: Nagarparkar is the gateway to pink granite mountains and hills of Karoonjhar that are quite different from the surrounding desert of Thar. The mountains are popular with hikers, there are several footpaths. Best time to visit if just after the monsoon season when the hills offer a lush green view.

name: Gurdwara Janam Asthan
content: A highly revered gurdwara that was built at the site where the founder of Sikhism, Guru Nanak, was believed to be born.

name: Dahi Bhale
content: these are delicious

name: Gol Gappe
content: these are really tasty. They are basically made with flour into a ball shape, and they are filled with black grams, onions, potatoes and other supplements. A sour drink called "khatta" is served with them. A number of gol gappay carts can be found, lined outside Station Park. Their dahi bhala fillings and dippings are unique and not worth missing

name: Biryani & Pulao
content: Biryani & pulao (special cooked rice) are also very popular

name: Dal Chawal
content: It's one of the favorite foods here

name: Rabri
content: this is the most favourite drink of the people of Nankana Sahib. It is made by mixing peanuts, almonds & many other dry fruits in milk and is very delicious

name: Sugar cane rusk
content: is also very delicious

name: Limo pani
content: is very tasty. It is made up with lemon juice & water

name: Lassi
content: Lassi is the traditional Punjabi drink.  Lassi is available in all parts of the city easily.  It is made using yogurt. The price of one glass or a Piala of Lassi is about Rs.20

name: River Whisper
content: Staff there can find you a shared jeep (i.e. for Rs 1500, 2025) to Saiful Muluk lake. You can have breakfast in the restaurant other side of the street.

name: Lalazar
content: N15, Main Bazar +92 997 430001

name: Kunhar View Hotel
content: Mansehra - Naran - Jalkhad - Chilas Rd, +92 333 5746739

name: New Sukoon Restaurant
content: A cosy restaurant in city serve some excellent and delicious meals in air-conditioned lounge. Have Pakistani, Continental, Seafood, Chinese dishes in menu as well as some Bar B Q and fast food along with fresh juices and plenty of desserts. Overall, a good place to dine in and is popular among locals.

name: Royal Taj Restaurant
content: Serve some excellent and delicious meals in air-conditioned lounge. Have Pakistani items like chicken chatni and karahi plus, BBQ, pizza, and fast food along with fresh juices and plenty of desserts. Overall, a good place to dine in.

name: Gym Khana Restaurant
content: A fine dining place in city, serve some excellent food, both Pakistani and Chinese and well popular among locals.

name: Peoples Continental Hotel
content: Have both air-conditioned and non air-conditioned rooms. attach baths, Free Wifi and have a good restaurant inside the hotel.

name: Sagar Hotel
content: Have both air-conditioned and non air-conditioned rooms. both Free wifi, attach baths, and has a good restaurant inside the hotel.

name: Gym Khana Guest House
content: Have 21 air-conditioned rooms with a good restaurant inside the hotel building. Hotel provide free Wifi, and rooms are with attach baths. Overall, ideal for stay.

name: Al Karim Hotel
content: A central air-conditioned hotel in centre of the city with only air-conditioned rooms, some are simple, some cozy. Very idea for stay overnight and female friendly hotel. Have security guards and Free Wifi.

name: Chaheen Jo Daro
content: is another archaeological site. It is near the village of Jamalkeerio 2 km from Rohri Canal and 10 km south of Nawabshah

name: Gorakh Hill
content: An under-development hill station on one of the highest plateaus of Sindh, at an elevation of 5,688 ft in the Kirthar Mountains Range. Due to the surroundings, it's a unique adventure point for nature lovers.

name: Shrine of Baba Fareed
content: One of Pakistan's most revered shrines. Built in the town that was known in medieval times as Ajodhan, the old town's importance was eclipsed by that of the shrine, as evidenced by its renaming to "Pakpattan", meaning "Holy Ferry" - referencing a river crossing made by pilgrims to the shrine. The shrine has since been a key factor shaping Pakpattan's economy, and the city's politics.

name: Tupopdan
content: is the striking mountain north of the town with many peaks, also known as 'Passu Cones' or  'Passu Cathedral'.

name: Views of the Hunza river
content: Passu is situated at a large meander in the river offering great views.

name: Borit lake and viewpoint
content: Access is from the town of Husseini, where a road traverses up the hillside. There is a campground and restaurant by the lake and you can swim in it during summer. If you continue on the road passed the lake you eventually get to the start of a trail that leads up the side of the Passu glacier offering perhaps the best views of the area

name: Suspension bridge
